correctness.rationale: For the repaired statement, positivity of λ ensures both bounded resolvents; multiplication by the continuous symbol has norm given by the scalar supremum. Scaling gives ε h(u−iξ), with h regular at zero and residue one at z=−2πin. Uniform convergence of u/ε on compact ξ-sets away from zero follows directly from the ordinary one-sided asymptotes, no derivative assumption. The prior strip estimate with (c*−η)|ξ|^α then bounds the full supremum, including escaping aliases, and the first center on a least-damped side gives the matching lower bound. In a fixed nonzero-alias neighborhood the principal part is ε/(u−i(ξ−2πn)) and the regular part O(ε), proving the locally uniform complex profile with the stated sign of iv and exclusion of larger displacements. The far-tail bound makes any maximizing sequence in ξ bounded; off-pole compact convergence forces nonzero alias limits. A peak has limiting modulus [c_s²(2π|n|)^(2α)+v²]^(-1/2); equality with the norm is possible only at |n|=1, c_s=c*, v=0. Conversely, o(ε) distance to the finite set of winning aliases gives ratio one by the uniform profile, also with equal damping and alternating signs. At fixed T and |y|→∞ the multiplier tends to T/2; the small-step peak exceeds it, hence is attained at a finite scalar frequency. This does not entail a norm-attaining vector in L². The frozen Python checker was inspected, not executed: it samples finite offsets and aliases, not the full supremum; the proof supplies all limits.
